co_palisade_mountain.blurb: Palisade Mountain is a large rocky mountain on the north side of Big Thompson Canyon in the Estes Park Valley, along US 34 near Drake, at about 7,400 feet. Slabs and crack systems dominate. Trad leads by a wide margin, with a smaller sport group plus some top-rope and a few boulders, and the rock is described as very solid. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, mostly 5.9 to 5.11. Approaches are steep and rough. Horseshead holds the most climbs, a roughly 250-foot spire with several multi-pitch lines, and Skull Rock faces south and takes full sun. Temple of Tao and Nancy's Rock are other crags.

nh_newmarket_durham.blurb: Newmarket and Durham, in the Seacoast corner of southeast New Hampshire, offer bouldering only. The problems are scattered in small pockets across a network of parks, conservation lands and town forests around the University of New Hampshire. Grades run from V0 to V6, with most problems at V0 to V2 and a smaller group in the harder range. Wiswall Boulders (aka Thompson Farm) holds the most climbs, with problems for beginners up through V6 beside the road. Sweet Trail Boulders lie along a hiking trail of about four miles, College Woods has limited but quality climbing, and Heron Point Sanctuary is a short session spot in downtown Newmarket on the Lamprey River.

or_m_smith_rock_group.blurb: Smith Rock Group is a massive block of rock south of Asterisk Pass at Smith Rock in Central Oregon, among the tallest portions of rock in the park. It holds a mix of old-school and modern multi-pitch climbs, with new routes added over recent years. Sport dominates, with a smaller trad share and a couple of top-rope lines. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.13, with most climbs at 5.10 and 5.11. Sectors circle from the east side near Asterisk Pass to the west. Northwest Face, Northeast Face and Llama Wall hold the most climbs. At Llama Wall the rock is pebbled and highly featured, and the routes are overhung.

sc_table_rock_state_park.blurb: Table Rock State Park, in the South Carolina Upstate, has two cliffs. Pumpkintown holds the most climbs; it is the southwest-facing cliff on the main escarpment, with climbs of one to seven pitches. The Table Rock cliff faces southeast to south, which makes it a good cold-weather option, and its routes are long and wandering face climbs on knobs, crimps, water grooves and slab. Many routes there offer little natural protection, and many run water after rain. Trad dominates, sport comes second, and grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, mostly 5.9 to 5.11.

tn_north_clear_creek.blurb: North Clear Creek is part of Obed & Clear Creek in Tennessee, with nine sub-areas. Across the Obed, the climbing is on steep, overhanging sandstone cliffs where the rock often leans past vertical. Here sport leads and trad is well represented. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, with the bulk at 5.11 and 5.12. Broom Wall/Rasputin Ledge holds the most climbs, with Squeeze Ledge, Sun Wall and Blue Crystal Buttress next. The area includes the shady coves of the Inner Circle and the roofs of the Rasputin Ledge.

va_lower_lightside.blurb: Lower Lightside is the lower zone of Jaybird Gorge in Southwest Virginia, holding boulders and roped routes of high quality. Lower Lightside Bouldering holds the most climbs, with 83 problems spread across 17 sub-areas. Most are V1 to V4, and the grades climb into the V8 to V9 range at the top. Lower Lightside Routes adds around 27 routes, almost all sport, with grades from 5.8 to 5.12 and clusters at 5.10 and 5.12.
